title: Al Cohn, Marilyn Moore and working at the Half Note
summary: Marilyn Moore connected him to Al Cohn, who gave him gigs, and later he played with Al and Zoot.

bands.name: Al Cohn and Zoot Sims band

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yes. Well, I went out to Al Cohn’s place in...

Great Neck? Yeah. Joe Cohn was on the floor, crawling around. Marilyn Moore, I had met her in Galveston and played behind her. She was my connection with Al. Al took me on right away, and he started giving me gigs. He wasn’t working much at that time. He was writing mostly on Broadway musicals. I later worked with Al and Zoot at the Half Note, but...
That was one of the things you enjoyed more than anything else, I think, was working with them.
Yeah. Paul Motian was there, and we made a record with Phil Woods and...
Yes. In 1959. Knobby Totah was on bass.
All right. Yes, Knobby Totah... Totah, we used to call it...
